## Carried here from PR #17137's contract review — three shipped sentences that claim load enforcement, and an assigned handoff that would otherwise be lost

`domain:engine` execution PM seat, `session_01XTBcV7zZHmokdyQgXjbyEU`, 2026-09-09T13:3xZ. Recorded now because Phase 1a's PR deliberately does **not** touch them, and the handoff naming their owner predates this card.

### The three carriers, located by the review on `8d1e62f3e`

| carrier | what it claims |
|---|---|
| `packages/core/src/security/plugin-permission-enforcer.ts:94-97` | *"The runtime calls this … so `SecurePluginContext` enforces exactly the consented surface"* — ⚠️ the **first half becomes true** when Phase 1a lands; the second half stays false until this card |
| `packages/spec/src/kernel/manifest.zod.ts:22-25` | *"the persisted `granted_permissions` set **enforced at load** by the PluginPermissionEnforcer"* |
| `packages/spec/src/kernel/manifest.zod.ts:703` (tombstone) | *"Use the permission declarations, which **are enforced**."* |

⚠️ ⛔ Re-locate every one by content — those line numbers are from another tree.

The third has a **coordination pin**: `plugin-runtime-tier-truthful-text.test.ts`, whose own text says it *"leaves the PERMISSIONS half … #11333 owns it"*.

### The handoff, which is the reason this comment exists

Comment `5469479175` assigned the correction to **"whichever dev executes #13457/#13458 … update the pin and the sentence together in that PR"**.

⇒ That instruction was written when #13457 was expected to deliver enforcement. It no longer does — #13457 is Phase 1a (the binding), and **this card is where enforcement arrives**. So the handoff's addressee is now this card, and ⛔ it would have been silently orphaned by the re-cut had it not been written down here.

⚠️ **Two of the three live in `packages/spec`**, which is the spec seat's surface. ⛔ Whoever takes this card does not edit them unilaterally — the pin and the sentence must move together, and the spec half needs that lane.

### Why they are not being fixed in Phase 1a

They are outside its declared surface, and — more to the point — **correcting them requires knowing what will be true**, which is this card's output. Rewriting them now would mean writing a second sentence that is true only after a card that has not been designed yet. ⛔ Phase 1a states plainly in its own body and changeset that it registers without enforcing; these three are the *pre-existing* claims it inherits, not ones it makes.

**Triage: lands on the ADR-0025 materialize seam (`SecurePluginContext` / `PluginPermissionEnforcer`); `domain:engine`; `priority:p1`.**

### Why p1

#13457 (now Phase 1a) binds an artifact's `grantedPermissions` to its plugins and hands each entry to `PluginPermissionEnforcer.registerGrantedPermissions` — a real deliverable, and the enforcer's first producer. ⚠️ But its own round **measured that Phase 1 as scoped cannot enforce**. ⇒ read plainly: granted permissions are **registered and not refused**. A permission set that records what is allowed and denies nothing is a permission set in name.

⇒ p1 on that reading. ⚠️ **It is the filing seat's measurement, ⛔ not this seat's** — the dispatched dev must confirm the enforcement gap on today's tree **before building**, and a clean stop reporting "it does enforce" is a full success.

### ⛔ Fences — this is a permission boundary

- The **direction** is already ruled: this is Phase 1b of #11333, on the ADR-0025 seam. ⇒ implementing it is execution, ⛔ not a new decision.
- ⛔ **Do not widen what is permitted.** The deliverable is that the registered set starts refusing what it never authorised — ⛔ not a re-negotiation of which permissions exist, and ⛔ not a new grant shape. Anything that changes *what is allowed* rather than *whether the existing rule is applied* is the maintainer floor: stop and report.
- ⚠️ **Turning enforcement on will break callers that are relying on it being off**, possibly including in-repo examples and tests. That is the defect surfacing — ⛔ but it must be **enumerated in the PR body**, not discovered downstream. If the blast radius reaches shipped app behaviour, stop and report before landing.

⚠️ **Reported to the maintainer in this round's report** as a live permission-enforcement gap.

`Size/model suggestion:` L — a security seam with a real blast radius; ⛔ not a rung.
